01_hook: Scanned books are pictures of pages. Everything inside them is invisible.
02_search: Type what you remember. A woman reading a letter: Seurat's drawing, in MoMA's nineteen twenty-nine loan exhibition catalogue, page one twenty-five. The figure, the caption as printed, the record, and a link to the exact page of MoMA's own P.D.F.. Colophon did this for seven hundred and fifty-seven catalogues, seventy-seven thousand pages, with two Meta models.
03_sam: First, SAM three point one finds every picture: paintings, photographs, drawings, prints, sculpture, maps, diagrams. It runs at home, on two DGX Sparks and a forty-ninety, about a page a second per machine. All seventy-seven thousand pages in five hours, zero failures: ninety-three thousand figures.
04_reader: Then Muse Spark reads each page once, with the figures numbered, and returns what each one depicts and its printed caption, split into artist, title, year, medium and credit. One call per page, strict jason.
05_works: A city street at night: Van Gogh's café terrace. And because the captions are read, not guessed, a work can be followed across catalogues. Picasso's Green Still Life, reproduced six times between nineteen thirty-one and nineteen thirty-six, each a different plate. Redon's Silence, five. Say-zann's Bathers, four. Which catalogue reproduced a work, and on which page: that index did not exist.
06_identifier: The identifier reads a book's title page, copyright page and last pages, and returns a catalogue record with the page each field came from. Nothing is guessed: a field not printed comes back empty, with a note. Every I.S.B.N. is checksum-tested, and a record is verified only when Open Library's title for it matches the title page. Scored on all seven hundred and fifty-seven catalogues against MoMA's own record sheet, which the model never saw: title ninety-four percent, year ninety, publisher eighty-six, author eighty-five, I.S.B.N. ninety-two. It even corrects MoMA. This brochure is dated nineteen eighty-seven on the sheet; the copyright line and the exhibition dates say two thousand and five.
07_scale: It is Python and sequel-light: three small servers and a coordinator any G.P.U. can join. Reading a page costs half a cent, identifying a book three cents; all seven hundred and fifty-seven for twenty-three dollars. Fifty-three catalogues are indexed so far; the rest is a matter of running it. The code, every number, and the list of P.D.F.s to rebuild it are on GitHub.
08_close: Colophon. A library that knows what is on its pages.
